review_finding: Docker daemon can create the new container before docker run times out or returns nonzero; a created flag set only after CLI success skipped cleanup.

red.observed_fault: Only docker run was invoked after injected ambiguous launch failures; no inspect or cleanup occurred.

change: Always inspect the generated exact container name in finally after any launch attempt.
Bound cleanup inspect to 15 seconds; classify an explicit exact-name no-such-container/object response separately from daemon/access errors.
Before removal, validate inspected Name, UUID ownership label, network none, no port bindings, tmpfs database storage and immutable container ID.
Remove the inspected immutable container ID rather than a mutable name, then confirm no container with the exact run label remains.
Refuse all removals on mismatched ownership/isolation; preserve original launch error when no container exists.

new_fault_cases: CLI timeout after daemon creation still inspects and removes only the owned immutable ID
CLI nonzero after daemon creation still inspects and removes only the owned immutable ID
explicit absent container does not trigger remove and preserves launch failure
daemon inspect error is not mistaken for absence

limitation: Fault tests exercise the real rehearsal/cleanup control flow with injected Docker CLI results; they do not claim a new real daemon timeout or hosted restore occurred. Process termination that prevents Python finally execution still requires operator resource reconciliation.
